ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there is a rectangular coordinate system, and the origin is marked as O. An increasing line goes from lower left to upper right, passing through point B on the left side of the x-axis, the intersection point C in the second quadrant, and passing through point A near the positive half-axis of the y-axis; another decreasing line passes through the origin O and point C. From the figure it can be seen that triangle OBC is enclosed by segment OB on the x-axis, segment BC on the increasing line, and segment OC on the decreasing line. Reasoning: Point C is on the line y=-2x, and its y-coordinate is 4, so 4=-2x, giving x=-2, that is C=(-2,4). Point C is also on the line y=x+b, so 4=-2+b, giving b=6; therefore the increasing line is y=x+6. It intersects the x-axis at B: let y=0, giving x=-6, so B=(-6,0). Point Q(m,2) is located on the horizontal line y=2. The intersection of this horizontal line with the line y=x+6 on which side BC lies satisfies 2=x+6, giving x=-4; the intersection with the line y=-2x on which side OC lies satisfies 2=-2x, giving x=-1. To make Q inside triangle OBC and not on the boundary, m must be strictly between these two x-coordinates. Final answer: m∈(-4,-1).
